content.text: Now I'll check how many orders and order lines there are.
Too many to read wholesale; for Q1 I'll fetch the orders of Harbor Supplies (C-2).
For Q2 and Q3 I'll read the lines of orders O-1007 and O-1004.
For Q4 I'll use cypher to find open orders with a line whose product is in category `valves`, grouping by order to dedupe.

input.statement: MATCH (o:order)<-[:of_order]-(l:order_line)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status = 'open' AND p.category = 'valves' RETURN o.id, o.customer, o.total, count(*) AS n

content.text: To make sure status values are consistent (e.g. no "Open" variants), I'll aggregate orders by status.
Statuses are clean. For Q5 I'll group orders by their customer's country via cypher.

input.statement: MATCH (o:order)-[:placed_by]->(c:customer) RETURN c.country, count(*) AS orders, sum(o.total) AS total

content.text: Counts sum to 1500 and totals match the status aggregate (8,191,727.96). For Q6 I'll sum line quantities by product category on non-cancelled orders.

input.statement: MATCH (o:order)<-[:of_order]-(l:order_line)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' RETURN p.category, count(*) AS lines, sum(l.qty) AS units

content.text: To verify no lines were dropped by the join (e.g. missing product or order), I'll count lines on cancelled orders and lines lacking a product or order.

input.statement: MATCH (o:order)<-[:of_order]-(l:order_line) RETURN o.status, count(*) AS lines, sum(l.qty) AS units

input.where: product is null or order is null

content.text: All 4,468 lines join; non-cancelled units sum to 166,496, matching the category total. For Q7 I'll read the qty ranking five lines at a time, first page.
I'll continue with the cursor to read ranks 6–10.
Rank 10 has qty 90; I'll check whether other lines tie at 90, which would make rank 10 ambiguous.
No ties at the boundary. For Q8 I'll ask `query` for the shortest walk from customer C-4 (Kestrel Farms) to C-5 (Ostrava Machining) over all relations.
The refusal says `depth` needs `min`; I'll give every step `depth {min:1, max:8}` so they form one combined walk.
It treated the steps as a chain; the description says a single walk needs every step to start at depth 0, so I'll set `min: 0`.
That's a 6-hop chain, the minimum possible between two customers. For Q9 I'll find products with no order line using cypher's `NOT` pattern.

input.statement: MATCH (p:product) WHERE NOT (p)<-[:of_product]-(:order_line) RETURN p.sku, p.name, p.category, p.supplier ORDER BY p.sku

content.text: For Q10 I'll find German customers with lines of Italy-made products, grouped by customer and order status so I can distinguish cancelled orders.

input.statement: MATCH (c:customer)<-[:placed_by]-(o:order)<-[:of_order]-(l:order_line)-[:of_product]->(p:product)-[:supplied_by]->(s:supplier) WHERE c.country = 'DE' AND s.country = 'IT' RETURN c.id, c.name, o.status, count(*) AS lines

content.text: Every German customer appears. For Q11 I'll sum Kestrel Farms' (C-4) units by supplier, split by order status.

input.statement: MATCH (c:customer {id: $c})<-[:placed_by]-(o:order)<-[:of_order]-(l:order_line)-[:of_product]->(p:product)-[:supplied_by]->(s:supplier) RETURN o.id, o.status, p.sku, s.id, s.name, s.country, sum(l.qty) AS units

content.text: To guard against the decimal/number comparison misbehaving, I'll cross-check with `order_find` for open orders above 12000.00 and filter by IE customers myself.
Both reads agree on five orders. Some "open" orders date from early 2026, so I'll check the lake's aging rules in case any of them changes order status.

I answered all 17 questions. Every read was pinned to one snapshot of the store (position 6136), so the answers are consistent with each other. The store has 60 customers, 12 suppliers, 81 products, 1,500 orders and 4,468 order lines, and none of them are retired. Order statuses take only three values: open (460), shipped (885) and cancelled (155).

**Tool corrections along the way:**
